articles.title: GTA 6 launch day guide: release date, platforms, pre-load and download size
articles.dek: GTA VI arrives November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Here's when you can pre-load, how much space to clear, and what to sort out before launch night.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, November 19, 2026, after two delays that pushed it back from fall 2025 and then from May 2026. It's coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only. There is no PS4 or Xbox One version, and Rockstar hasn't announced a PC release.
## Pre-loading
If you bought the game digitally, pre-loading has been open since November 10, so you can download it now and play the moment it unlocks. Boxed copies work differently: the box holds a download code rather than a disc, and those codes became available from November 12.
## Clear some space
The download is large, up to 212 GB depending on your console. That's a big chunk of a standard PS5 or Series X drive, so check your free space before launch night rather than during it. An approved expansion drive is worth considering if you're short.
## The pre-order bonus
Anyone who buys before November 20 gets the Vintage Vice City Pack, which includes a classic '55 Vapid Stanier sedan, a garage, outfits for both leads and a weapon pattern. Digital buyers also get a free month of GTA+. See our editions guide for the full breakdown.
Work through the checklist below before launch night. It remembers what you've ticked in this browser.
checklist: Confirm your copy is bought (digital or boxed code)
Redeem your boxed download code, if you have one
Free up around 212 GB of storage
Install the latest console system update

articles.title: GTA 6 Standard vs Ultimate Edition: what the extra $20 gets you
articles.dek: The Standard Edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99. Both play the same story. Here's what the upgrade adds and who it's worth it for.
articles.body:
Rockstar is selling two versions of GTA VI. Both contain the full game and the same story. The difference is a bundle of extra single-player items that come with the Ultimate Edition.
## What every pre-order gets
The Vintage Vice City Pack comes with any copy bought before November 20, Standard or Ultimate:
- A '55 Vapid Stanier sedan and a Shore Court garage with a weapon locker and a drop-off point for fencing goods
- Retro outfits and hairstyles for Jason and Lucia
- A tropical palm-tree pattern for most weapons
- One free month of GTA+ on digital pre-orders
## What the Ultimate Edition adds
- Extra vehicles, including a '95 Grotti Cheetah, a '67 Vapid Dominator buggy with its own garage, a Shitzu Squalo boat, a Dinka Enduro bike and a kayak
- Extra revolvers and personalized versions of two pistols
- Vice City-style outfits and tattoos
- Two extra pieces of content: a raid on a PTT Youngin$ compound and a classic-car job for a character named Wyman
- Access to five shops: Rideout Customs, Sara's Unisex Salon, Stock 305, Electric Fang Tattoo and One-Eyed Willie's
## Our verdict
For most players, the Standard Edition is enough. The Ultimate items give you a head start on cars, guns and style, but none of it changes the story. The Ultimate Edition is digital only, so if you want a box on the shelf, Standard is your only choice. And there's no rush: Standard owners can buy the Ultimate upgrade later if they decide they want it.

articles.title: Jason Duval
articles.dek: One of GTA VI's two playable leads: an Army veteran from a family of hustlers, doing jobs for drug runners in the Keys and looking for a way out.
articles.body:
Jason is one of the two characters you play in GTA VI. Rockstar's profile describes a man who grew up surrounded by grifters and small-time crooks, joined the Army to get away from a rough youth, and came home to find the same life waiting for him. These days he does work for drug runners in the Keys.
## What we know
- He lives in a property owned by Brian Heder, an old-school smuggler, and helps Brian out in return.
- His friend Cal Hampton is part of the same circle around Brian.
- His relationship with Lucia Caminos is at the heart of the story. The trailers frame them as a criminal couple, and many fans compare them to Bonnie and Clyde.
- The trailers suggest the pair end up working with veteran bank robber Raul Bautista.
## Still to come
Rockstar hasn't explained how switching between Jason and Lucia works or which missions belong to whom. We'll add his story missions, safehouses and key moments to this page after launch, with spoilers hidden behind a tap.

articles.title: Lucia Caminos
articles.dek: GTA VI's other lead: a fighter fresh out of Leonida Penitentiary, chasing the better life her mother wanted for the family.
articles.body:
Lucia is GTA VI's second playable character, and the first woman to lead a GTA game in the modern era. Her father taught her to fight from a young age. According to Rockstar's profile, that toughness landed her in Leonida Penitentiary after she fought for her family, and she got out partly through luck.
## What we know
- Her family's story stretches back to Liberty City, the series' take on New York. Her mother has wanted a better life for them ever since.
- She and Jason are a couple, and the game is built around the two of them deciding how far to go together.
- The trailers show her alongside Jason in heists and robberies, apparently including jobs set up by Raul Bautista.
## Still to come
We'll add her story missions, key choices and side content after launch. Major plot points will be hidden behind a spoiler tap, so you can read this page safely at any point in the game.

articles.title: Cal Hampton
articles.dek: Jason's homebody friend, who'd rather sit at home with a beer, eavesdrop on the Coast Guard and read up on conspiracy theories.
facts: Listening in on Coast Guard radio
articles.body:
Cal is Jason's friend and another member of Brian Heder's circle in the Keys. Where Jason wants something bigger, Cal is happy where he is: at home, with a few beers, listening to Coast Guard radio traffic and browsing the stranger corners of the internet.
## What we know
- Rockstar plays him as the paranoid one, the kind of guy who half-believes everything he reads online.
- Monitoring Coast Guard communications would be a handy skill for anyone moving goods by boat, which hints at how he might help the crew.
- His comfortable routine looks likely to be disrupted once Jason and Lucia's plans pick up speed.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll note the missions Cal appears in and anything he unlocks, such as information, jobs or equipment.

articles.title: Boobie Ike
articles.dek: A Vice City street legend who turned his earnings into real estate, a strip club and a recording studio, and now wants a hit record.
facts: Real estate, strip club, recording studio
articles.body:
Boobie Ike is one of Vice City's best-known faces. He made his name on the streets, then turned that money into a business empire that looks legitimate from the outside: property, a strip club and a recording studio.
## What we know
- His biggest passion project is Only Raw Records, the label he runs with Dre'Quan Priest, a hustler with music-mogul ambitions.
- The label has signed rap duo Real Dimez and is chasing its first real hit.
- Rockstar presents him as self-interested but invested in Dre'Quan's success, which could make for an interesting partnership as the label grows.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add his missions, businesses you can visit and any jobs he offers.

articles.title: Dre'Quan Priest
articles.dek: A dealer with music-mogul ambitions, partnered with Boobie Ike at Only Raw Records, who has just signed Real Dimez.
articles.body:
Dre'Quan sold drugs to get by, but music was always the goal. He's spent time booking performers into Boobie Ike's strip club, and now he's partnered with Boobie on Only Raw Records.
## What we know
- He signed rap duo Real Dimez to the label, his first big move.
- With a real act on his books, he's setting his sights on Vice City's wider music scene, which may mean less time working for Boobie's club.
- That ambition could put him at odds with Boobie, though Rockstar hasn't said how the relationship plays out.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add the missions he's involved in and any music-business side content.

articles.title: Real Dimez (Bae-Luxe and Roxy)
articles.dek: High school best friends turned social media rap duo, newly signed to Only Raw Records after an early hit with local rapper DWNPLY.
articles.body:
Real Dimez is a duo: Bae-Luxe and Roxy, friends since high school. They built a following on social media and through their rap tracks, and before music took off they made money working with local dealers.
## What we know
- An early single with local rapper DWNPLY gave them their first taste of success.
- They're now signed to Only Raw Records, run by Dre'Quan Priest and Boobie Ike.
- Their story looks set to explore the pressure of going from internet fame to a real career, with plenty of temptation along the way.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add their missions and anything else they unlock.

articles.title: Raul Bautista
articles.dek: A charming, seasoned bank robber who recruits people for risky jobs, which seem to grow more reckless as the game goes on.
facts: Appears to work with Jason and Lucia
articles.body:
Raul is a career bank robber with plenty of experience and plenty of charm. He's always looking for capable people willing to take risks, and the jobs he plans pay well but carry real danger.
## What we know
- Rockstar describes his jobs as increasingly reckless, which suggests anyone working for him will eventually have to decide whether to push their luck or walk away.
- A scene in the second trailer appears to show Jason and Lucia as part of his crew.
- If GTA VI has big, planned heists like earlier games, Raul looks like the most likely person to set them up.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add his heist missions with approach options, crew choices and payouts, written to help you pick the best route.

articles.title: Brian Heder
articles.dek: An old-school smuggler from the Keys' glory days who still moves product through his boatyard, and Jason's landlord.
articles.body:
Brian ran drugs during the golden age of smuggling in the Keys and never really stopped. He still moves product through his boatyard, though these days he prefers to have other people do the dirty work.
## What we know
- Jason lives in one of Brian's properties and does jobs for him in return.
- Cal Hampton is one of his associates.
- His third wife, Lori, works with him at the boatyard.
- He's one of the first faces you see in the second trailer, which suggests he plays an early role in Jason's story.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add the jobs Brian gives you, where to find his boatyard, and how his story connects to the main plot.

articles.title: Vice City
articles.dek: Leonida's neon-lit centerpiece, with art deco hotels on Ocean Beach, the busy streets of Little Cuba and a cruise port that calls itself the capital of the world.
facts: Ocean Beach, Little Cuba, VC Port
articles.body:
Vice City returns as the heart of GTA VI. It's a modern take on the series' classic Miami-style city, swapping the 1980s for the present day while keeping the sun, the neon and the excess.
## Places to know
- Ocean Beach, with white sand and pastel art deco hotels
- Little Cuba, a compact, busy neighborhood of narrow streets
- VC Port, which bills itself as the cruise ship capital of the world
## Getting around
Raised freeways and crowded streets make the city slower to cross than the open countryside. Previews suggest that breaking line of sight will matter more than raw speed when you're trying to lose the police here.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll map Vice City's shops, safehouses, side activities and the best escape routes.

articles.title: Leonida Keys
articles.dek: A laid-back island chain of boat parties, dive bars and reef diving. It's also Jason's home turf.
articles.body:
The Leonida Keys are a string of tropical islands south of the mainland, with an easygoing pace to match. It's where Jason lives and works, so expect to spend a good part of the early game here.
## Places to know
- The Rusty Anchor, one of the dive bars Rockstar has highlighted
- Bays full of boat parties
- Brian Heder's boatyard, the base of his smuggling business
## Things to do
Scuba diving is one of the confirmed activities, with turtles and other sea life to find, along with some hazards beneath the surface. With so much water around, boats will be one of the best ways to get around.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add dive spots, boat locations and any Keys side jobs.

articles.title: Grassrivers
articles.dek: Leonida's vast wetlands, full of stilt houses, mangroves, alligators and stranger things hidden in the water.
articles.body:
The Grassrivers are GTA VI's version of the Everglades: miles of marsh and mangrove forest, with buildings on stilts along the edges. It's a world away from Vice City's streets.
## What to expect
- Alligators are the headline attraction, and the area is a hunting spot
- Rockstar warns of deadlier predators below the surface and some disturbing discoveries deeper in
- Other people out here hunting are likely to be armed, so don't assume a quiet swamp is a safe one
## Getting around
Airboats look like the natural choice for crossing the water, and fans have spotted a hovercraft in the trailers.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add hunting spots, hidden locations and any wetland side quests.

articles.title: Port Gellhorn
articles.dek: Leonida's forgotten coast: a faded resort town of empty strip malls and run-down motels, where the drug trade is filling the gap.
facts: Decline, with a new drug economy
articles.body:
Port Gellhorn used to be a tourist destination. Now its glory days are long gone, and what's left is a stretch of tired motels, abandoned attractions and empty strip malls.
## Places to know
- The Starlet Motel
- The Delights cabaret
- Deserted strip malls and closed-down attractions
## What's happening here
Rockstar says the drug trade has moved in to fill the economic gap, creating a new local economy. That points to plenty of criminal opportunity on Leonida's west coast.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add Port Gellhorn's businesses, side jobs and points of interest.

articles.title: Ambrosia
articles.dek: An industrial town by Lake Leonida, built around the Allied Crystal sugar refinery and run by a local biker gang.
articles.body:
Despite the sweet name, there's little sweet about Ambrosia. It's a working industrial town beside Lake Leonida, and most people here depend on the Allied Crystal sugar refinery that dominates the skyline.
## What to expect
- Old-fashioned blue-collar values, enforced by the biker gang that controls the area
- Factories, rail yards and heavy industry rather than beaches
- A very different crowd from Vice City, so expect different kinds of jobs and trouble
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add Ambrosia's missions, the biker gang's role and what's worth visiting.

articles.title: Mount Kalaga National Park
articles.dek: The wild northern border of Leonida, home to hunting, fishing, kayaking, off-road trails and some deeply suspicious locals.
articles.body:
Mount Kalaga National Park forms Leonida's northern edge, a big stretch of forest and hills for anyone who wants to get away from the city.
## Things to do
- Hunting, with deer and mountain lions mentioned by Rockstar
- Fishing and kayaking
- Off-road trails for trucks and bikes
## Who lives here
The backwoods are home to hermits and paranoid types hiding from the government. Some will make for strange encounters, and some may be dangerous.
## Still to come
After launch, we'll add the best hunting grounds, trail routes and any secrets hidden in the park.
